$comment: Gemfall beat 2, The Fork. Story: docs/campaigns/gemfall.md §2. Wiring: docs/campaigns/gemfall-authoring.md. Must set on every path to every ending: exactly one of sprites_friends / sprites_wronged (decided on the branch that resolves the Harvest Stone, below choice_harvest_stone, which every path passes through) and exactly one of route_river / route_rush / route_wild (on the three choices out of choice_rumour_board into the three endings). Expanded for pacing: every path walks the stopped song, Hob's verse, the egg stall, the plank bridge, the night shiver, the corner row, the hedgehog signpost, Pib's gift and Marda's common room; none of these set route-set flags.
title: Green Roads North

objectives.label: Walked the rows instead of through them
Fed the cold wolves instead of fighting them

facet_harvest.name: The Harvest Stone
facet_harvest.text: A green-gold stone from a sprites' corner row. It still wears a tiny medal: BEST.

medal_not.name: A Very Small Woven Medal
medal_not.text: Woven by harvest sprites for leaving their stone alone. It says NOT.

scene_song_stops.narration: The caravan cook pushes a supper bundle into your pack "for the road, crew," and the caravan rolls through the Sunward Fields, and in every field the fauns are singing their work-songs. Then, halfway through a verse, every song stops at once. A faun with an irrigation flute freezes so suddenly that the flute keeps watering her hoof. Every Sunward child knows what a stopped song means: somebody has seen something worth stopping for.

choices.label: Look where the fauns are looking
Ask the faun with the flute what she saw

scene_song_stops_look.narration: You shade your eyes and look down the lane. A cloud of dust is rolling toward the next field, and the dust is full of wagon wheels. Rush wagons, lots of them, and they are not slowing down. Way out in the pumpkins, something tiny in an acorn helmet is watching them too, with its arms folded.

choices.label: Run to the pumpkin field

scene_song_stops_ask.narration: You tap the faun on the shoulder. She jumps, notices her wet hoof, and turns the flute off. "Wagons," she whispers. "Rush wagons, heading for the pumpkins." Then, because you asked so nicely, she pulls a spare reed whistle out of her hat. "For when you need everybody to hear you. One loud note, mind. It only has the one."

choices.label: Run to the pumpkin field

scene_trampled_field.narration: The road ahead is jammed with gem wagons, so a rush caravan has decided to drive straight through a field of pumpkins that nobody has harvested yet. A faun foreman called Hob Thistledown waves his hat at you. "Help us turn them," he says, "before they make soup of the whole season!"

choices.label: Talk the drovers round
Walk the rows to find a way around
Stand in the road and roar, politely
Stand in front of the wagons. Somebody has to

scene_trampled_field_duty.narration: You plant your feet in the road in front of the lead wagon and do not move. The oxen stop with their noses touching your coat. The drover shouts. You stay. A pumpkin rolls out of the field, bumps your boot, and stays too, as if it has joined you. The drover throws up her hands and turns the oxen.

choices.label: Lead the wagons round the edge

scene_trampled_field_roar.narration: You step into the road, clear your throat, and roar. It is a polite roar, the kind with a please in it, and it still rattles the pumpkins. Every ox in the caravan sits down at once. The drover looks at her oxen, looks at you, and decides the field can keep its pumpkins.

choices.label: Lead the wagons round the edge

check_reroute.prompt: Talk a grumpy drover out of a shortcut

onSuccess.narration: You ask the drover how she would feel about a wagon parked on her dinner. She thinks about it, then turns her oxen.

onFailure.narration: The drovers don't listen. Three wagons cut a muddy stripe right through the squash before the rest swing round. A faun starts singing a very sad verse about it.

scene_walk_rows.narration: You walk the rows instead of through them, hopping between pumpkins like stepping stones, and find a cart track around the edge of the field. Something tiny in an acorn helmet pats your boot, very approvingly, and is gone before you can look properly.

choices.label: Lead the wagons round the edge

scene_caravan_turned.narration: The rush caravan rumbles off around the field, grumbling. The fauns start singing again from exactly where they stopped, and Hob adds a new verse with your names in it. He presses a warm honeycake into your hands. "For the road," he says. "It's getting crowded out there, all the way to Bramblewood."

choices.label: Walk on with Hob to the crossroads
Sing Hob's new verse back to him

scene_caravan_turned_onward.narration: Hob walks you to the crossroads, telling you the life story of every pumpkin on the way. The biggest one is called Gerald. At the crossroads he stops and sniffs. "Eggs," he says, and his face goes serious. "Listen. Whatever the rush is paying for eggs today, a neighbor should not have to." Then he waves his hat until he is just a dot.

choices.label: Follow the smell of eggs

scene_caravan_turned_sing.narration: You sing the verse back to Hob, names and all. You get the tune wrong in two places and the words wrong in three. Hob is delighted anyway. He teaches you the proper way, and then the whole field sings it at you, twice, until you could sing it in your sleep. "Now you're Sunward," says Hob. "Any faun who hears that verse will help you."

choices.label: Back to the road north

scene_egg_stall.narration: At the crossroads, a faun is selling eggs from a cart. Her price board has been rubbed out and written higher so many times it is mostly smudge. Every rush wagon that rolls past leans out, pays whatever she says, and takes the lot. At the back, a faun dad with three small kids is counting coins that are not enough for one egg anymore. A hen on the cart looks offended by all of it.

choices.label: Help her work out a fair price
Buy eggs for the family at the back
Get the rush buyers into a proper queue
Haggle with the rush buyers like an Exchange trader

check_egg_price.prompt: Work out a price that is fair to the neighbors and to the rush

onSuccess.narration: You do the sums on the back of the price board. Two prices, you decide: one for the rush, and one for neighbors. The egg faun reads it twice and laughs out loud.

onFailure.narration: You do the sums three times and get three different answers. The last one says an egg costs one duck. The hen does not like that at all.

scene_egg_price_fair.narration: The new board says RUSH PRICE in big letters and NEIGHBOR PRICE in small ones. The rush buyers grumble and pay, because they are in a hurry. The faun dad buys a whole dozen at the neighbor price. The egg faun chalks your names in the corner of the board, so the next wagon knows exactly who to blame.

choices.label: Back to the road north

scene_egg_price_muddle.narration: The egg faun laughs so hard she has to sit down on the cart. "I can't do the sums either," she says. "So I'll do the easy thing." She sells the faun dad his eggs for his old coins, the same as last year, and charges the next rush wagon double for being rude. The hen settles back down, satisfied.

choices.label: Back to the road north

scene_egg_stall_buy.narration: You pay the rush price, which makes your purse a lot lighter. The faun dad tries to say no, then says thank you three times instead. The smallest kid unties a ribbon from her little horn and ties it on your sleeve. It has a songbird stitched on it. "Now you have to sing," she says. So you do, badly.

choices.label: Back to the road north

scene_egg_stall_queue.narration: The kitsune hops up on the cart and calls out, very grandly, "The queue starts here!" Rush folk cannot resist a queue. Twelve buyers line up behind the faun dad without knowing why. By the time they reach the front, he has his eggs at the old price, and the egg faun is charging the queue a little extra for the fun of standing in it.

choices.label: Back to the road north

scene_egg_stall_haggle.narration: You lean on the cart like a trader from the Exchange and start naming prices. Huge ones. The rush buyers argue, then pay, then thank you for the bargain. The egg faun's purse is so full it clinks when she breathes. She gives the faun dad his eggs for nothing, and gives you a wink that says she knows exactly what you did.

choices.label: Back to the road north

scene_jackalope_road.narration: Next, the road is full of jackalopes. Hundreds of them. Usually they race the wagons and win, but today they are just sitting, packed in tight on the open road, every ear pointed the same way: inland, toward the long grass. A jackalope only crowds the road when something on the other side of the grass is worth being able to see coming. Up on the low ridge above the road, a flock of sheeple stands in one woolly knot, all staring the same way.

choices.label: Look where the jackalopes are looking
Fly up and look over the long grass
Visit the flock on the ridge

scene_flock_ridge.narration: On the low ridge above the road, about thirty sheeple are standing in one tight woolly knot. Every one of them is wearing the same felted hat with seven brims. When you walk up, nobody says anything for a whole minute, because each sheeple is waiting for another one to say hello first. Then twenty of them say hello at once. "What do we think?" asks the one in the middle. "We think wolves," they all answer, slightly out of step. "In the grass." "We all saw them." "Because one of us did."

choices.label: Crouch down and look where they're looking
Stroll into the middle of the flock
Wave goodbye and go back to the road

scene_flock_bigfoot.narration: Nobody bolts. Nobody even flinches. The whole flock shuffles in around the bigfoot and leans on them like a warm, woolly wall, and a calm flock notices things. It notices, without anybody saying a word, who the clever one is. Thirty heads turn to watch them.

choices.label: Let the clever one crouch and look

check_flock_clever.prompt: Look closely enough that a whole flock decides you are worth copying

onSuccess.narration: You crouch, and you squint, and you tilt your head. Thirty sheeple crouch, squint, and tilt their heads exactly the same way. The flock has decided you are clever. Nobody told it to. It just knows.

onFailure.narration: You crouch down. The flock watches you politely and does not crouch. Then a jackalope bursts out of the grass right beside you, and that is the end of the meeting.

scene_flock_copies.narration: Thirty pairs of eyes see a lot more than one pair. Down in the long grass are two cinder wolves, and they are not hunting. They are shivering, and they have been staring at the caravan's sausage wagon since breakfast. When you stand up to go, three sheeple in seven-brimmed hats stand up too. They follow you down the ridge at a very polite distance, and they stop whenever you stop.

choices.label: Head down toward the wolves, with company

scene_flock_scatters.narration: The flock scatters in threes, every three running a different way. Then each little three stops, throws back its head, and calls the Gather. You can't hear a thing. It looks like thirty sheeple yawning at the sky in perfect silence. A minute later they are all back in one woolly knot, pretending nothing happened. One of them points at the long grass, just to be helpful, and you see two gray shapes lying in it.

choices.label: Thank the flock and go and see

scene_jackalope_road_fly_look.narration: From above, the long grass is a green sea, and two gray shapes are lying in it like boats, perfectly still, each with a faint orange glow under the fur. Mountain wolves. In farm country. One of them looks straight up at you and does not even pretend it isn't there.

choices.label: Land and tell the others

scene_wolf_sign.narration: In the dust by the long grass are big paw prints, and the prints are still warm. Caught on a thistle is a tuft of charcoal fur with a faint glow under it. Cinder wolves, mountain wolves, all the way down here in the farm country. Two of them are lying in the grass, shivering, watching the caravan's sausage wagon the way you might watch a birthday cake.

choices.label: Leave your supper bundle out and back away slowly
Shoo them away from the wagons
Hurry the caravan on, very quietly

check_wolf_kind.prompt: Put down your supper bundle without looking like a snack

onSuccess.narration: The wolves eat every crumb and the sausage too, curl up into one warm gray heap with eight legs, and watch you go. They are not tame. But they will remember you.

onFailure.narration: You trip over your own supper bundle. The wolves decide you are part of the offer.

encounter_wolves.narration: Two cold cinder wolves slink out onto the road, glowing faintly, more hungry than angry.

onVictory.narration: The wolves back off into the long grass, ears down, looking more embarrassed than anything. They are a very long way from home.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves knock you flat, grab the whole sausage wagon's worth of sausages, and trot off, warmer and happier. It takes you half the afternoon to re-pack the wagons, and supper is very short on sausages.

scene_plank_bridge.narration: Late in the afternoon the road crosses an irrigation canal on a little plank bridge. Or it did. A rush wagon too heavy for it has cracked the middle plank right through, and the fauns on the far bank cannot bring their hay carts home. One of them is throwing hay bales across, one at a time. Most land in the water. A duck is riding one, looking very pleased with itself.

choices.label: Heave a new beam into place
Carry the hay across, one bale each
Hold the bridge up on your shoulders
Sing Hob's verse across the canal

check_bridge_beam.prompt: Lift a fence post the size of a canoe and drop it in exactly the right place

onSuccess.narration: Heave. Shove. Thump. The new beam drops into place with a sound like a door shutting. The first hay cart rolls over, and the bridge does not even creak.

onFailure.narration: Heave. Shove. Splash. The beam slides off the bank and into the canal, and floats there. The fauns look at it. Then they look at each other.

scene_bridge_mended.narration: The fauns roll every hay cart home over your bridge, singing the whole way. One of them carves a little pumpkin on the new beam, for luck. Down in the long grass beside the canal, something tiny in an acorn helmet stands up, salutes you very smartly, and disappears.

choices.label: On down the road

scene_bridge_ferry.narration: The fauns tie a rope to each end of the floating beam, and just like that, the canal has a ferry. They pull the hay across one cart at a time, cheering every trip. The duck rides along on every single one. "Better than a bridge," says a faun. "A bridge never goes anywhere."

choices.label: On down the road

scene_plank_bridge_carry.narration: You wade in and carry the hay across, one bale each, over and over. It takes ages. Everybody sneezes. By the end the far bank is empty, the near bank is stacked high, and everybody looks like a scarecrow. A jackalope hops past wearing a little hat of hay and does not seem to know.

choices.label: On down the road

scene_plank_bridge_shoulders.narration: The bigfoot steps down into the canal and puts their shoulders under the cracked plank. The bridge lifts back level. "Go on," they say. Cart after cart rolls over their head, and the fauns pat the bigfoot's hair as they pass, very respectfully. The duck sits on top of the bigfoot the whole time, like a hat.

choices.label: On down the road

scene_plank_bridge_sing.narration: You sing Hob's verse across the canal, names and all. On the far bank every faun stops. Then they sing it back, louder, and come splashing across with a spare plank from the barn, still singing. The bridge is mended before the last verse ends. The duck does not join in, but it nods along.

choices.label: On down the road

scene_embermoths.narration: At sunset a cloud of embermoths drifts overhead, thousands of them, glowing like slow sparks. One lands on your soup and will not get out. But the cloud is drifting south, toward the sea and away from the mountain, which is the wrong way entirely.

choices.label: Say out loud that this is impossible
Rescue the embermoth from your soup
Watch them go, and then get some sleep

scene_embermoths_soup.narration: You fish the embermoth out with a spoon. It sits on the spoon, steaming gently, and will not leave. It is as warm as a cup of cocoa. When the rest of the cloud has gone, this one is still here, glowing on the rim of your cup all through supper. At bedtime it tucks itself in beside you.

choices.label: Get some sleep

scene_embermoths_watch.narration: You lie back in the grass and watch the cloud go by. It takes a long time. Thousands of little lights drift over, south and south and south, until the sky is dark again. Far away to the north, the mountain still glows red, and not one moth is flying toward it. Then you get some sleep.

choices.label: Sleep

scene_impossible.narration: "That's impossible," says the dragonling. "Embermoths go toward warm. Always. The mountain is the warmest thing there is. Back home the grandmothers would be ringing the bells." Nobody laughs. A little embermoth settles on the dragonling's horn, as if to say: tell them again.

choices.label: Get some sleep

choice_night_tremor.narration: In the middle of the night the ground gives a small shiver. The cups rattle on their hooks. The wagon bells ring once, all together. Every jackalope in the field sits up with its ears straight. Then it stops, as if it never happened. Everybody is wide awake now. What do we do? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Put an ear to the ground and listen
Roll over and go back to sleep
Hold the warm red stone from the Exchange
Watch the little embermoth

check_tremor_listen.prompt: Lie very, very still and hear what the ground is saying

onSuccess.narration: You press your ear flat to the cold ground and hold your breath. Far, far away, there is a sound.

onFailure.narration: You press your ear flat to the ground and hold your breath. The only thing you can hear is the caravan cook, snoring.

scene_tremor_heard.narration: It is one long, low note, deep under the fields, coming from the north. It is not a rumble. It is more like a hum, very old and very slow. Then it fades, and the crickets start up again. You lie awake for a long time, listening for it to come back. It doesn't.

choices.label: Try to get some sleep

scene_tremor_snore.narration: The cook snores like a kettle. Then like two kettles. Then, right in the middle of a big snore, the ground gives one more tiny shiver, and the cook says "Pass the gravy" in her sleep and carries on. You give up and go to sleep. Whatever the ground wanted to say, it has said it.

choices.label: Get some sleep

choice_night_tremor_sleep.narration: You pull the blanket over your head and sleep like a log. In the morning everything looks normal. Except the cups. Every cup in the whole camp has shuffled off its hook and over to the north side of the table, all lined up and all facing the same way, as if they wanted a better look.

choices.label: Pack up and set off

choice_night_tremor_stone.narration: You take the warm red stone out of your pack. It is humming. You feel it more than hear it: one low note, very old and very slow, buzzing in your fingers. When the ground goes still, the stone goes still too, as if the two of them had been talking and have just stopped. You put it away very carefully.

choices.label: Try to get some sleep

choice_night_tremor_moth.narration: The little embermoth beside you has woken up. Its glow pulses, bright, dim, bright, as slow as breathing, and every pulse comes with a shiver you can only just feel through the blanket. When the shivers stop, it dims and goes back to sleep. By morning it has flown away south, after the others.

choices.label: Get some sleep

scene_corner_row.narration: In the morning, near the last farm before Bramblewood, there is one corner row nobody has picked. Every farmer knows to leave the corner rows, and nobody says why. Today the row is guarded. Four harvest sprites in acorn-cup helmets stand to attention, and every time a pea-pod trumpet toots, four new ones march in to take their places.

choices.label: Creep closer and see what they're guarding
March up and salute the guard
Wave hello, like the bridge menders we are

scene_corner_row_closer.narration: You creep between the cabbages on tiptoe. You get very close. Then a sprite in a bean-pole lookout tower spots you, toots the pea-pod trumpet twice, and the whole guard spins round. Nobody charges. They just look at you, hard, the way a librarian looks at someone eating crisps. Then they step aside, so you can see.

choices.label: See what they are guarding

scene_corner_row_salute.narration: You march up the row and salute. The four guards salute back so hard that one of them falls over. Then the whole rotation is introduced to you, one sprite at a time, with their rank, their favorite vegetable, and how many medals they have. It takes a while. At last they step aside, very proudly, so you can see what they are guarding.

choices.label: See what they are guarding

scene_corner_row_wave.narration: You wave. Every sprite in the row waves back at once. "The bridge ones!" one of them shouts. "The bridge ones are here!" A pea-pod trumpet plays a little fanfare. Two sprites carry a tiny bench out of the cabbages so you can sit down, even though it is much too small for anyone. Then they lead you to the middle of the row.

choices.label: Follow them to the middle of the row

choice_harvest_stone.narration: In the middle of the row sits a green-gold stone the size of a hen's egg. Somebody has pinned a tiny woven medal on it that says BEST. It fell from the sky into the sprites' row, and they have decided that makes it theirs, very seriously. What do we do?

choices.label: Offer them a trade
Offer to help tidy their row
Grab it while the guard changes
Leave it where it fell
Wait quietly. The sprites already know us

check_trade.prompt: Offer the sprites the best thing in your pockets

onSuccess.narration: You offer a shiny button, a song, and your very best joke. The sprites go into a huddle. They come out of the huddle. It's a deal.

onFailure.narration: The sprites look at your offer for a long four seconds. Then they point, all together, at the weeds in the row. They don't want things. They want help.

check_earn.prompt: Pick up every dropped seed before the sprites do

onSuccess.narration: It's a race, and it was always a race. You win by one seed. The sprites are thrilled, and tuck a honeycake into your pocket for later.

onFailure.narration: The sprites beat you to every seed, and you get stung by a nettle on the last one. But you worked till lunchtime without complaining, and the sprites decide that counts.

check_steal.prompt: Snatch the stone between one trumpet toot and the next

onSuccess.narration: Toot. Swap. Snatch. You are gone before the new guards reach their spots. Nobody saw. Probably.

onFailure.narration: You grab it, and the trumpet toots the alarm. Forty sprites riding jackalopes chase you down three rows and through a nettle patch before you get away.

scene_medal_ceremony.narration: There is an award ceremony. Attendance is mandatory. The best beetroot gets a medal, the best bean gets a medal, and then the sprites hand you the Harvest Stone, medal and all. They make you promise to keep it somewhere with a nice view.

choices.label: On to Bramblewood

scene_stolen.narration: The stone is in your pack. Behind you the corner row has gone very, very quiet. Every sprite in the field has stopped tidying to look at you. Nobody says anything. Harvest sprites do not need to say anything. Harvest sprites remember.

choices.label: On to Bramblewood, quickly

scene_leave_it.narration: You leave the stone exactly where it fell. The sprites look at each other. Then they hold a second, smaller ceremony and pin a very small woven medal on you. It says NOT. Nobody explains.

choices.label: On to Bramblewood

scene_signpost.narration: On the last stretch to Bramblewood the road splits three ways, and the signpost at the fork has so many signs nailed to it that it looks like a hedgehog. GEMS THIS WAY. NO, THIS WAY. BRAMBLEWOOD (PROBABLY). SHORTCUT!!! The rush has written its hopes on every board. The real sign is somewhere underneath. A jackalope sits on the very top, enjoying the view.

choices.label: Find the real sign under all the others
Follow the wagon ruts. Everybody else went this way
Wave down the egg cart
Climb the signpost and direct the traffic

check_signpost.prompt: Peel off the rush's signs without bringing the whole post down

onSuccess.narration: Board by board, you peel the rush's signs away. Underneath, carved deep and very old, is the real one.

onFailure.narration: You pull one sign too many. Every board slides off at once and lands in a heap, all pointing different ways. You pick the biggest.

scene_signpost_found.narration: The real sign says BRAMBLEWOOD on one arm and FIELDS on the other. The third arm has no words at all, only a carved row of corn with one corner left empty. Nobody knows what that means. You lean the rush's signs neatly against the post, so nobody's hopes get trodden on, and take the Bramblewood road. It is quiet and green, with hardly a wagon on it.

choices.label: On to the hedges

scene_signpost_lost.narration: The biggest sign says GEMS THIS WAY. It leads to a duck pond. The ducks have clearly seen a lot of rush folk today and are not impressed. A faun fishing at the edge points you back the right way without being asked, and only laughs a little. By teatime you can see the hedges.

choices.label: On to the hedges

scene_signpost_ruts.narration: The wagon ruts are deep and easy to follow. Everybody went this way. Absolutely everybody. The ruts lead you up one hill and down another and straight into the back of a very large crowd, outside a very tall hedge. You have found Bramblewood. So has everyone else.

choices.label: Squeeze through to the hedges

scene_signpost_cart.narration: The egg cart rattles up behind you, and the egg faun waves you aboard. "Neighbor price," she says, "which is free." She takes a farm lane the rush has never heard of, and the hen rides on your lap the whole way, which is an honor. She drops you right at the hedges, then rattles off to sell eggs to the crowd. At the rush price.

choices.label: On to the hedges

scene_signpost_direct.narration: You climb to the top of the signpost, next to the jackalope, and start pointing. Wagons this way. Walkers that way. Nobody through the fields, please. You look so official that the rush does exactly what you say. One drover even thanks you. When you climb down, the jackalope stays up there, pointing at nothing, in charge.

choices.label: On to the hedges

scene_hedge_mob.narration: Outside Bramblewood's tall hedges, a mob of treasure hunters is camped and shouting, "Open up! Let us through!" The hedges are not listening. Along the wall, a small thorny sprite with a satchel too big for them is trimming one leaf at a time and narrating it. "I'm Pib," they say. "I can't let them in. The hedges don't listen to people who haven't asked properly. What about you?"

choices.label: Tell Pib honestly why we've come
Help Pib trim the hedge first
Shout with the crowd, louder!
Show Pib the sprites' medal
Bow to the hedge and ask, the way the flock would

scene_hedge_mob_flock.narration: You step up to the hedge and bow. Far back from the shouting, the three sheeple bow too. Then all three throw back their heads in perfect silence. For a minute, nothing happens. Then sheeple start arriving at the edge of the clearing: ten, twenty, thirty, all in the same hat, all bowing to the hedge at once. "Please may we come in," they say, slightly out of step. The mob is so surprised it stops shouting. Pib drops their shears. The hedge has never been asked that politely by that many people, ever. It opens a path wide enough for {party}, and the flock trots in too, very pleased with itself.

choices.label: Follow the flock up the lane

scene_hedge_mob_cousins.narration: Pib sees the sprites' medal and gasps. "Cousins! You've met my cousins!" The hedge opens before Pib has even finished the sentence, wide enough for a cart, and a thorn reaches out and very gently straightens the little medal.

choices.label: Walk in like you were expected

scene_hedge_mob_help_pib.narration: You take a brush each and trim with Pib, one leaf at a time, for a very long time. Pib narrates all of it. Somewhere around the four hundredth leaf, the hedge gives a long rustle, like a cat deciding to like you, and a small gap opens at exactly your height. The mob does not notice. Pib is beside themself with pride.

choices.label: Slip through the gap

check_hedge.prompt: Say why you came, plainly enough for a hedge to hear

onSuccess.narration: The hedge rustles, thinks about it, and quietly opens a path just wide enough for you and nobody else. The mob doesn't even notice. Pib looks very proud of the hedge.

onFailure.narration: You mean it, but it comes out sounding like a speech. The hedge has heard a lot of speeches this week.

scene_long_path.narration: Pib sighs and offers you a thorn-cleaning brush you did not ask for. "Let's try again. Properly." You say sorry to the hedge. The hedge accepts, slowly: the path it opens winds back and forth eleven times, and by the time you reach the other end the mob outside has shouted itself hoarse.

choices.label: Finally, into town

choice_pib_gift.narration: Inside the hedges, Pib trots up the lane beside you, narrating every leaf on the way. At the door of the inn they stop and dig in the big satchel. Out come three things you did not ask for. "I can only spare one," says Pib. "The hedge says you should choose it together." Which one? Everybody vote.

choices.label: The thistle pin, for being prickly when it matters
The owl feather the hedge was keeping safe
The pebble with a hole in it, for luck

choice_pib_gift_pin.narration: Pib pins the thistle on your coat and steps back to admire it. "Prickly," they say, satisfied. "But only on the outside. Like a hedge." The thistle stands up very straight, as if it is proud to be chosen.

choices.label: Go into the inn

choice_pib_gift_feather.narration: Pib hands over a soft gray owl feather on a little clasp. "An owl left it in the hedge in the spring," they say, "and the hedge has been keeping it for somebody clever. The hedge thinks it might be you. It isn't sure." The feather tickles. It seems to be thinking it over.

choices.label: Go into the inn

choice_pib_gift_pebble.narration: Pib drops a smooth pebble with a hole in it into your hand. "For luck," they say. "When things go wrong, you look through the hole, and they go a bit less wrong. That's how I do the tricky bits of hedge." Pib shows you by looking at you through it, very seriously, for a long time.

choices.label: Go into the inn

rest_marda_inn.narration: Marda Thorn's inn has doors wide enough for a centaur, and Marda still ducks under them out of habit. She brings stew and does not hurry you. Everyone in the common room is arguing: crystal deposits here, a blocked road there, tremors where there shouldn't be any. Nobody agrees on anything except that the rumor board is where you decide.

choices.label: Eat your stew and listen to the arguing
Show Marda the warm red stone from the Exchange
Ask Marda which rumor she believes

rest_marda_inn_show_ember.narration: Marda takes the warm red stone in one big hand and holds it to her ear. The common room goes quiet. The stone hums. "Mm," says Marda, and gives it back, and wipes her hand on her apron as if the hum might come off. Then she asks the one question she asks everybody this season.

choices.label: Hear her question

scene_marda_question.narration: Marda pulls up a stool, which creaks. "Here is what I ask everybody this season," she says, and waits for the whole answer: "Where is it all going?" She doesn't mean the road. "Me, I believe all three rumors," she adds. "That's the trouble with this season."

choices.label: Listen to the arguing

choice_common_room.narration: After supper the common room gets louder. Three tables are arguing louder than all the rest. At the window, a frogfolk ferrier with reeds in her hat. By the hearth, a centaur relay runner, muddy to the knees. By the door, a dusty rush drover eating three dinners at once. You can only listen properly to one table. Which one? Everybody vote.

choices.label: The frogfolk ferrier at the window
The relay runner by the hearth
The drover by the door
Tell the room about the hum under the fields

choice_common_room_frog.narration: The frogfolk ferrier tells it slowly, like a story. West, the Whispering Marsh is busy for the first time in a hundred years. Her cousins pole the travelers they like, and leave the rude ones on a nice little island to think about it. "The marsh whispers more at night now," she says. "But if it likes you, it's the gentlest road there is."

choices.label: Go and read the rumor board

choice_common_room_runner.narration: The relay runner talks fast, the way runners do. East, the queue at Stone Crossing is moving again, slowly. The trolls there take a story instead of coins, and a river drake is charging double to anyone who won't wait. "Past the river it's all open country," she says. "You can see trouble coming a day away. Doesn't mean you can stop it."

choices.label: Go and read the rumor board

choice_common_room_drover.narration: The drover talks with her mouth full. North is the shortest road, straight up through the Plains, and the whole rush is on it, wheel to wheel. Campfires every night. Songs. Somebody selling something at every bend. "You don't walk the Rush Road," she says. "You fall in, and it carries you. Mostly to the ford. Then you wait."

choices.label: Go and read the rumor board

choice_common_room_tremor.narration: You tell the room about the shiver in the night, and the long low hum under the fields. The room goes quiet. The frogfolk felt it in the reeds. The relay runner felt it on the road. The drover's teacups all shuffled north in the night. Nobody laughs. Marda sets down her tray and says nothing at all, which, from Marda, means a great deal.

choices.label: Go and read the rumor board

choice_rumour_board.narration: Marda's rumor board is notes pinned on top of notes, and three fresh ones are underlined twice. EAST: The crossing queue is moving again! NORTH: Rush road jammed but MOVING. Fall in and be carried! WEST: Frogfolk still ferrying them they like. "The north road's shorter," says Marda. "Shorter isn't quicker." Which way? Everybody vote.

choices.label: East to Stone Crossing: the River Road
North with the rush: the Rush Road
West into the marsh: the Wild Road

end_river.narration: East, then. Marda chalks your names under EAST, and in the morning you'll take the Sunward road to the Great River, where the trolls want stories instead of coins. Tonight you sleep in a real bed for the first time since the Exchange. Somewhere far off, you can almost hear the river.

end_rush.narration: North, then, straight up the middle with everybody else. Marda chalks your names under NORTH, right at the bottom of a very long list. Tonight you sleep in a real bed while the wagons creak past the hedges all night long, and every one of them is going your way.

end_wild.narration: West, then, into the reeds where hardly anybody else is going. Marda chalks your names under WEST, where there is lots of room. Tonight you sleep in a real bed. Out past the hedges, the marsh frogs sing very loudly, as if somebody has already told them you are coming.

llmHints.tone: warm green farm country with something wrong at the edges; funny, kind, a little uneasy, never scary
forbidden: explaining why the embermoths are flying the wrong way
naming a sheeple, or showing fewer than three

npcVoices.hob: Hob Thistledown, a faun field foreman; warm and half-singing, turns every answer into an anecdote, waves his hat a lot
npcVoices.sprites: harvest sprites; tiny, earnest, over-explaining, very serious about guard duty and award ceremonies, heartbroken by a refusal for about four seconds
npcVoices.pib: a bramble sprite the size of a teapot who keeps the hedges; earnest, narrates their own maintenance, offers you things you did not ask for, cannot open the hedges for anyone who has not asked properly
npcVoices.marda: Marda Thorn, a gray-dappled centaur innkeeper; unhurried, asks one question and waits for the whole answer, never repeats herself
npcVoices.drover: a grumpy rush-caravan drover in a hurry who is, underneath, fond of her dinner
npcVoices.sheeple: a flock of sheeple, never fewer than three and never named; warm, agreeable, and in chorus, checks with the others first ("What do we think?"), answers in three voices slightly out of step, finishes each other's sentences, skittish but never silly
npcVoices.flute_faun: the faun with the irrigation flute; startled, whispery, generous to anyone polite
npcVoices.egg_faun: a faun egg-seller at the crossroads; laughs easily, cannot do sums, fierce about neighbors paying neighbor prices
npcVoices.cook: the caravan cook; only ever talks in her sleep, about gravy
npcVoices.ferrier: a frogfolk ferrier with reeds in her hat; slow, storytelling, fond of the marsh and politely firm about rude passengers
npcVoices.relay_runner: a muddy centaur relay runner; talks fast, plain, practical, has seen the whole road east
